text: Body builds can be sorted by overall effect: well-proportioned; tall, thin and angular; short, round and stout; broad-shouldered and narrow-hipped; or stooped.
quote: Is it well-proportioned? Tall, thin, and angular? Short, round, and stout? Broad-shouldered, narrow-hipped? Stooped?

text: A heavy-footed walk reads as heavier, a soft-soled springy step as lighter, and a hard-heeled walk as more authoritative.
quote: Shoes with soft soles create a lighter, more resilient step; hard-soled shoes, especially those with heavy heels, produce a more authoritative walk.

text: Walking in high heels adds swing to the hips and thrusts the pelvis forward, changing posture and balance.
quote: High-heeled shoes create a walk with more swing in the hip, and the posture and balance of the figure must be adjusted.

text: In middle age women's breasts begin to sag and men's muscles become soft and less defined.
quote: Women’s breasts begin to sag, and men’s muscles become soft and less defined.

text: Elderly figures stand about 7 to 7.5 head-lengths tall.
quote: Aged characters are drawn at 7 to 7 1/2 heads high.

text: Disease and old age make the figure stoop and shrink.
quote: Disease and old age can cause stooping and shrinking of the figure.

text: When the shoulders and back are strongly bent with age, the knees bend to keep balance and the head is thrust back to see forward.
quote: If the shoulders and back become quite bent, the knees must bend to prevent the figure from falling forward.

text: Very old people may be thin and frail with soft muscles and sagging skin.
quote: Extremely old people may be thin and frail with soft muscles and sagging skin.

text: The neck, elbows, knees and torso, soft and rounded in youth and middle age, become bony with age.
quote: The neck, elbows, knees, and torso, which in youth and middle age have firm muscles and fatty tissue to give them soft, round shapes, become bony with age.

text: In elderly women the breasts sag more and the buttocks become flat.
quote: In women the breasts sag more and the buttocks become flat.

text: Weight settles first around the waist for most body types, which in men usually means a belly.
quote: Weight settles first in the waist area for most body

text: Women gain weight in the waist, stomach, hips and breasts, and with more weight the thighs and upper arms become heavy.
quote: weight in the waist, stomach, hips, and breasts. As weight increases, thighs and upper arms become heavy.

text: Excess weight rounds the shoulders, shortens the neck, makes limbs rounded rather than muscular and makes legs look shorter.
quote: Excess weight has the effect of rounding shoulders and shortening the neck. Limbs are rounded, not muscular. Legs appear shorter.

text: When weight shifts onto one leg, the body's center line tilts off vertical, running from the pit of the neck through the crotch down the non-supporting leg.
quote: When the weight of the figure is shifted to one leg, the center of the body is no longer perpendicular to the base of the sketch.
